Article Title: ‘Speedy trial is a fundamental right’: SC says Constitution has primacy over special laws
Article Text:
Supreme Court of India

'

Speedy trial

is a fundamental right, can't tinker'

SC: Constitution should be guide to interpret law, not the other way round

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Should fundamental rights take precedence over special laws like NDPS and UAPA? Definitely. No, special laws should prevail. Depends on the individual case. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Constitution will prevail over all other laws and regulations, Supreme Court said on Thursday and made it clear that in case of any contradiction or conflict between constitutional provisions and special laws like NDPS, UAPA and PMLA, it is the former which will triumph.It reiterated that the right to speedy trial was a fundamental right and could not be violated under any law and could be the ground for bail.The bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A S Chandurkar faulted the apex court's earlier order, which held that under special statutes such as NDPS Act, an accused's right under Article 21 (speedy trial) must be exercised within the confines of Section 37 of the Act (stringent bail conditions) and cannot be invoked solely on the ground of prolonged delay to override Section 37.The latest ruling comes amid sharp differences within the apex court over granting bail in PMLA, NDPS and UAPA cases on grounds of delay in trial, with the issue now before a larger bench.Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A S Chandurkar also said fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under the special statutes.The bench said, "First and foremost, the rights conferred by Article 21 of the Constitution are not only constitutional rights.These are fundamental rights. Right to life and liberty as enshrined in Article 21 are at the core of our constitutional jurisprudence. These fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under the special statutes."Such observations run counter to numerous judgements of this court which reiterate the proposition that when there is a violation of Article 21 of the Constitution, the rigour of Section 37 of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act or similar such provisions under special statutes would have to give way, the court said.The court's observation assumes significance as there are differences of opinion within Supreme Court on the issue of bail in offences under Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), NDPS and Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) on grounds of delay in trial. Contradictory orders have been passed on whether the fundamental right to have a speedy trial would prevail over stringent bail conditions stipulated under special laws, with one bench saying the right to speedy trial cannot be the ground to grant bail in PMLA, UAPA offences while other benches took contradictory stands.The controversy now stands referred to a larger bench after two benches took swipes at each other in their judicial orders. "A statute, special or otherwise, cannot be a guide to interpret the Constitution; rather, it should be the other way round. To reiterate, a fundamental right must be interpreted in such a manner that it upholds and furthers the objective of such a fundamental right," the bench said, adding, "The court must interpret the Constitution in a manner which would enable citizens to enjoy the rights guaranteed by it in the fullest measure. "
Article Summary: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A S Chandurkar said fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under the special statutes. Ruling comes amid sharp differences within the apex court over granting bail in PMLA, NDPS and UAPA cases on grounds of delay in trial.

Article Title: Iraq airspace available again, Air India flights between Delhi, Mumbai and New York become nonstop; shave 4 hours off from Rome one-stops
Article Text:
Air India

NEW DELHI: In a “Diwali gift” to travellers, Air India has once again made its flights between Delhi/Mumbai and New York (JFK and Newark EWR) nonstop since Wednesday, shaving close to four hours from the travel time of the one-stops these had become since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb 28. The airline's operations team, like that of other carriers, does constantly analyses enroute geopolitical situation and as soon as the risk rating for Iraq, Syria and Jordan reduced, it has started got a slightly shorter route available making the flights between Delhi and EWR; Delhi and JFK; Mumbai and EWR and Mumbai and JFK nonstop once again, skipping the Rome Fiumicino stop. Now the journeys become 15-16 hours, instead of the almost 20 hours they took with the Rome stop.The closure of Pakistan airspace since last April had made routes longer between Delhi and the west but the Iran airspace was open till Feb 28 when the US-Iran war broke out. Since then, the non-availability of Iran, Iraq and other enroute airspaces forced fuelling stops to be added. Now while Iran remains out of bounds, the Iraq airspace has become available and AI flight operations has seized the opportunity to make the New York flights nonstops again.While no one knows when and if Pakistan airspace will reopen for Indian carriers, AI is hoping that Iran airspace opens so that it can add more nonstops to the west. As of now in the current situation, its flights between Delhi/Mumbai and New York are likely to remain nonstop in Nov and Dec. From Jan, the winds become very strong and if the loads are high then fuelling stops may return for some time.“There is load penalty (restriction in number of passengers and/or cargo to carry more fuel for longer routes) since Pakistan airspace closed. So that remains. What has changed for now is that Iraq has become available again and made the flights nonstops again,” said pilots who operate this route.With the devastating economic impact of the US-Iran war on the midterms and Republicans facing a rout there, there is hope that the war will come to an end. If that happens, AI will add much more capacity to the west, including North America.
Article Summary: Air India has once again made its flights between Delhi/Mumbai and New York (JFK and Newark EWR) nonstop since Wednesday. The airline's operations team, like that of other carriers, does constantly analyses enroute geopolitical situation. As soon as the risk rating for Iraq, Syria and Jordan reduced, it has started got a slightly shorter route.

Article Title: 24-hour deadline starts with detention: SC
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday ruled that the constitutional mandate of producing an arrestee before a magistrate within 24 hours starts the moment one is detained for interrogation and not from the time when formal arrest is made by an investigating agency, since the liberty of a person is curtailed when one is detained.Noting that no artificial distinction should be created between detention and arrest, a bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar quashed the verdicts of high courts which had held that the 24-hour period starts only after formal arrest and not during antecedent detention necessitated by statutory procedure of seizure. Article 22(2) mandates that every person who is arrested and detained in custody has to be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of such arrest."Article 22(2) does not sanction exclusion of the time taken for enquiry and investigation before the arresting authority could effect arrest of the detainee. This is beyond the mandate of Article 22(2) of the Constitution. Article 22(2) does not sanction creation of any buffer zone where the liberty of an individual is curtailed for investigating purposes but not formally shown as arrested. Creation or contemplation of such buffer zone is unconstitutional..." the bench said.As it is common practice for police to record formal arrest much later, sometimes even a day after detaining a person for interrogation, Supreme Court's order would serve as a check on the police and other investigating agencies. The court also noted that its order was meant to eliminate custodial violence, which unfortunately takes place during the time when a person is under detention and not shown as formally arrested, in the process delaying production before the magistrate.
Article Summary: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar quashed verdicts of high courts. High courts had held that the 24-hour period starts only after formal arrest. The court also noted that its order was meant to eliminate custodial violence.

Article Title: Government buys time on UGC rules without committing to withdrawal or retention
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Centre's move to consider a fresh review of the controversial UGC equity regulations are being seen as an olive branch to agitating upper caste groups, while giving BJP room to avoid a fresh caste controversy ahead of the assembly elections, particularly in Uttar Pradesh.The regulations, which extended specific protection against caste-based discrimination to OBCs alongside SCs and STs, had triggered protests among general category students who feared exclusion and possible misuse of the provisions.Centre told Supreme Court Thursday that it was contemplating setting up a committee to reconsider the regulations, ensuring that no section of students felt excluded or apprehensive. The move gives govt time to revisit the issue without committing itself to either withdrawing or retaining the rules.A complete rollback has been a key demand of upper caste organisations, whose protests also caused unease within BJP. Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh have been leading govt's outreach to agitating youth outfits. Both had met representatives of Kshatriya Karni Sena-led 'UGC Rollback Campaign' in Sept, after which a proposed mahapanchayat was postponed.The Jan notification had caused resentment among sections of general category students who felt the regulations portrayed upper castes as the principal perpetrators of caste discrimination. The absence of a specific provision against false complaints added to their concerns.At the heart of the controversy is the wording of the regulations. While one provision defines caste-based discrimination specifically as unfair treatment of SC, ST and OBC members, another prohibits discrimination against any student, including on caste grounds.General category students argue that this creates confusion over whether they would receive the same protection if they face caste-based discrimination.Supporters of the regulations argue that historically disadvantaged communities need specific safeguards against discrimination.For BJP, a complete withdrawal carries political risks. OBCs and Dalits form an important part of its social coalition, especially in Uttar Pradesh, where caste identities remain politically sensitive.
Article Summary: The regulations extended specific protection against caste-based discrimination to OBCs alongside SCs and STs. Centre told Supreme Court Thursday that it was contemplating setting up a committee to reconsider the regulations. The move gives govt time to revisit the issue without committing itself to either withdrawing or retaining the rules.

RAIPUR: Tents, music, food and cars. Then came the roosters and the bets running into lakhs. Once a Maoist-controlled stretch of forest in Bastar, the remote terrain had acquired a different notoriety - an interstate cockfight gambling carnival attracting punters from across Chhattisgarh and neighbouring Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.Police busted the den near Raiguda village under Bhadrakali police station limits deep inside Bijapur district on Nov 3, catching 156 people and seizing more than Rs 20 lakh, 47 four-wheelers and 12 mobile phones.Acting on intelligence inputs about large-scale betting being organised under the cover of traditional cockfights, police cordoned off the forest site before moving in. Article Title: 'Memory of the world': Rajatarangini, Mahabharata & Arthashastra get UN recognition
Article Text:
The decision was taken at the 11th session of the Memory of the World Committee for Asia and the Pacific (MOWCAP), held in Jakarta, Indonesia.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Three major works of India's literary, historical and intellectual heritage, Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata' and Kautilya 's 'Arthashastra', have been added to Unesco's Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific.The decision was taken at the 11th session of the Memory of the World Committee for Asia and the Pacific (MOWCAP), held in Jakarta, Indonesia.The development was announced by Dr Sachchidanand Joshi, member secretary of the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), which contributed to preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.In 2024, India had secured regional register recognition for three other literary works: The Ramcharitmanas, Panchatantra and Sahṛdayālokalocana.With the latest additions, India's total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six.Composed in the 12th century, Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini' provides a chronological account of Kashmir's rulers, political developments and the region's social and cultural life. Its approach to documenting history through evidence, traditions and critical inquiry gives it a distinct place in Indian historiography.The 'Mahabharata', one of the major epics of Indian civilisation, explores themes including Dharma, duty, justice, power and human relationships. Its philosophical reflections and enduring values have also made it part of South Asia's shared cultural memory.Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' deals with governance, statecraft, economic policy, diplomacy, administration and strategic affairs. The work reflects ancient India's political and administrative thinking and its understanding of the functioning of the state.The three inscriptions represent different aspects of India's intellectual traditions, spanning historical writing, philosophy and ethical thought, and governance.The announcement also comes amid efforts under the Gyan Bharatam Mission to preserve, promote and digitise India's manuscript heritage. The initiative aims to identify, conserve and digitise manuscripts across the country and make them accessible to future generations and the global community.
Article Summary: Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata' and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' have been added to Unesco's Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the memory committee in Jakarta, Indonesia. The announcement comes amid efforts under the Gyan Bharatam Mission to preserve, promote and digitise India's manuscript heritage.

Article Title: NC rebellion calms down at Abdullahs’ door; Omar’s advisor Wani is in London as Speaker accepts Ruhullah’s resignation

SRINAGAR: Ruling National Conference rebel legislators, who are seeking the replacement of all eight Cabinet ministers, including the deputy chief minister, within 15 days and the removal of chief minister Omar Abdullah ’s adviser Nasir Aslam Wani, after meeting party president Farooq Abdullah and chief minister Omar Abdullah at the former’s residence in Srinagar said the party has agreed to implement some of the “confidence-building measures and suggestions they had put forward. ”“In today's meeting we decided that some of the confidence-building measures and suggestions we had put forward would be implemented soon, while others would be taken up gradually. You will see that in the coming days,” Bashir Ahmad Veeri, MLA from Bijbehara said after coming out of the meeting.“We are committed to Article 370 (restoration) and we will remain committed to it. It took the BJP to declare it done and dusted almost 70 years. Our fight (for its restoration) has not even completed four years yet,” he added.“We are committed to J&K's autonomy within the Indian federation on the basis of which Jammu and Kashmir acceded to India...you will see in the coming days how aggressively we pursue the restoration of statehood,” he added.Dismissing the reports of divisions within the party, he said, “The reports suggesting that the National Conference is divided in factions or that the party is on the verge of a split are completely wrong.The party is united and strong. Those who think they can break the party will never succeed. The party will neither split nor be weakened.""At the same time, our fight for the restoration of statehood. We will take this struggle to its logical conclusion,” he said, adding that the party fight for restoration of Article 370 will continue."Earlier the legislators were seen arriving at Farooq Abdullah’s residence around 11 a.m. Nazir Ahmad Khan an MLA from Gurez constituency, who is believed to be leading the dissenting legislators, said Dr Abdullah was their leader and they had come to meet him with their grievances.For the past one week, Omar faces a growing revolt within NC, with around 25 legislators demanding replacement of all eight cabinet ministers and removal of Wani. Wani is seen very close to the CM and legislators’ complaint that Wani is taking all important decisions of the Omar government despite being not elected.The MLAs’ meeting took place followed Omar’s cabinet expansion last week, triggering open dissent, protests and allegations of internal bias in NC after four ministers were inducted, taking the cabinet’s strength to nine, including the CM. He dropped Satish Sharma, leaving only two ministers from Jammu region-deputy CM Surinder Choudhary and Javed Ahmed Rana. NC has 41 MLAs in the 90-member assembly and runs a coalition government with six Congress, six independent and one CPM legislator.Incidentally Wani, whom legislators want out, is away from the political developments around him and is currently in London. Wani is part of Jammu and Kashmir Tourism delegation participating in the World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026. The WTM held at ExCeL London from November 3 to 5, had dedicated stalls showcasing the J&K’s diverse tourism offerings and emerging opportunities. The Indian Pavilion at WTM London was inaugurated by Union Minister of Tourism, Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, in the presence of Wani. Wani is expected to be back to Srinagar on Nov 10.This dissidence with the NC has come at a time when the party’s Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi ended on November 3 his 24-year association with NC, resigning as its functionary and Srinagar MP while declaring his exit an act of "azadi" and accusing CM Omar of betraying the party's election promises, surrendering to BJP and failing to defend J&K's political rights. In his November 3 speech Mehdi recalled the 2024 assembly election campaign in Ganderbal and said Omar had removed his skullcap and sought votes in the name of its dignity."You remember nothing, neither your promises nor your skullcap,"' he had said.His resignation as Member of Parliament from the Srinagar Lok Sabha constituency, has been formally accepted by the Lok Sabha Speaker, bringing his tenure as a Lok Sabha member to an end with effect from November 3, 2026.According to an official notification issued by the Lok Sabha Secretariat and published in the Gazette of India on November 5, 2026, Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi, an elected member representing the Srinagar Parliamentary Constituency of Jammu and Kashmir, has resigned from his seat in the Lok Sabha. The notification, states that his resignation has been accepted by the Speaker with effect from November 3, 2026. With the acceptance of his resignation, the Srinagar parliamentary seat has formally fallen vacant.
Article Summary: Ruling National Conference rebel legislators are seeking the replacement of all eight Cabinet ministers, including the deputy chief minister. They also want the removal of chief minister Omar Abdullah ’s adviser Nasir Aslam Wani. Wani is away from the political developments around him and is currently in London.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday announced the annual Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim.The poll roll revision exercise seeks to enrol eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors, and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1 and Oct 1, 2027. In this special edition of the Knowledge Series, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, speaks with impact catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka about her understanding of Ashtalakshmi, the power of the human mind, and why she believes that the journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 must begin within each of us.Aruna Lohia Goenka: (Laughs) Oh, Sanjiv! If money were the only measure of wealth, some of the richest people in the world would never feel poor! A person may have a magnificent home but no peace of mind. Another may have modest possessions but extraordinary courage, wisdom, loving relationships and a deep sense of purpose. Who, then, is truly wealthy? Our tradition offers a beautiful answer through Ashtalakshmi, the eight manifestations of Goddess Lakshmi.Aruna Lohia Goenka: (Smiles) In a sense, yes. We spend so much of our lives searching outside for what may already exist as potential within us. I do believe in magic. The magic of the universe. But I don't mean sitting back and waiting for miracles. I mean aligning our thoughts, intentions and actions with the possibilities around us. The universe may offer extraordinary possibilities, but we must do our part to recognise and realise them. And that brings me to the eight Lakshmis.Aruna Lohia Goenka: The wealth of knowing who we truly are. Adi Lakshmi reminds us that beneath our names, professions, and possessions lie the Atman, our deeper spiritual self. Spiritual wealth begins when we stop asking only, "What do I have?" and start asking, "Who am I?" To activate Adi Lakshmi, cultivate self-awareness, reflection, gratitude and inner stillness by spending time with your own consciousness. After all, what is the point of conquering the world if we remain strangers to ourselves?Aruna Lohia Goenka: (Laughs) Of course! Money is a wonderful servant, though it can become a rather demanding master! The real question is not how much wealth we accumulate, but how much good that wealth enables us to do. To activate Dhana Lakshmi, create wealth ethically, manage it wisely and allow it to circulate for the benefit of others. Money becomes truly meaningful when it moves from money to meaning.Aruna Lohia Goenka: Food and nourishment are central to Dhanya Lakshmi, but I also see in her a larger lesson about abundance. Dhanya Lakshmi reminds us to value nourishment, nature's bounty and the dignity of having our basic needs fulfilled. To activate this manifestation, practise gratitude, avoid waste and ensure that the abundance we enjoy reaches others.Aruna Lohia Goenka: Through leadership with grace! To me, true royalty is not about a throne or a title. It is about how you conduct yourself, especially towards people who have less power than you. To activate her, cultivate humility and generosity. A title may give you authority. But only your conduct can give you stature.Aruna Lohia Goenka: Yes. I see Santaaan Lakshmi as the wealth of continuity, and responsibility towards future generations. What do we pass on to our children and those we mentor? Only possessions? Or also intellectual curiosity, spiritual awareness, and the confidence to lead meaningful lives? To activate Santaaan Lakshmi, nurture physical, intellectual and spiritual well-being not only in ourselves but also in those whose lives we touch. And remember, the greatest inheritance is not necessarily what we leave for our children, but what we awaken within them.Aruna Lohia Goenka: Ah! That is when we need Veera Lakshmi. Courage is a form of wealth that no bank can lend us. To activate her, we must learn to confront fear rather than surrender to it. Not to let fear make our decisions. Sometimes the greatest victory is simply refusing to give up when everything around us says we should.Aruna Lohia Goenka: Vidya Lakshmi (learning and wisdom) improves our judgement and helps us navigate life with equanimity. To activate Vidya Lakshmi, remain curious, question assumptions, and share what you discover. The truly educated person is not who claims to know everything, but the one who never stops learning.Aruna Lohia Goenka: Yes, but I believe the greatest victories are often invisible. I associate Vijaya Lakshmi with overcoming the five vikars: kama (uncontrolled desire), krodha (anger), lobha (greed), moha (attachment) and ahankara (ego). These are battles we encounter in everyday life. To activate Vijaya Lakshmi, practise self-mastery, humility, compassion and conscious living. Conquering the world may bring applause. Conquering yourself brings freedom.Aruna Lohia Goenka: By recognising that national transformation begins with individual transformation! Imagine a Bharat where people consciously activate these eight dimensions within themselves. Imagine these qualities being expressed not merely by a few exceptional individuals, but by hundreds of millions of people. That is how a national vision becomes a lived reality.Aruna Lohia Goenka: To awaken the eight Lakshmis within you. Don't merely pray for abundance. Become a source of abundance! We need to embrace all eight manifestations to build Viksit Bharat. And these eight Lakshmis are not somewhere beyond our reach. Their potential lies hidden in every corner of Bharat, within every one of us. We must feel it, believe it and, above all, activate it together!I believe in the magic of the Universe. Think of each contribution as a drop of water. Every drop we contribute can become part of an ocean. But why stop at imagining one ocean? We are a nation of 1.4 billion people. Imagine 1.4 billion individuals, each becoming an ocean of wisdom, courage, compassion, knowledge and generosity! 1.4 billion oceans, flowing together towards Viksit Bharat 2047. That is the magic I believe in!
Article Summary: In this special edition of the Knowledge Series, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, speaks with impact catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka about her understanding of Ashtalakshmi, the power of the human mind. She believes that the journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 must begin within each of us.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi gets relief as Allahabad HC rejects plea seeking FIR over remarks on Sikh community

NEW DELHI: The Allahabad high court on Wednesday declined to interfere with a Varanasi court order rejecting a plea seeking registration of an FIR against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on India's Sikh community during a visit to the US in 2024.Justice Vikram D Chauhan dismissed the application filed by the petitioner, Nageshwar Mishra, observing that the allegation against Rahul Gandhi was based solely on newspaper reports about his statements during his US visits, which did not specify the date, time or place of the remarks."In such a situation, no order directing registration of a case against a person can be passed," PTI quoted Justice Chauhan as saying.Mishra approached the high court after the Varanasi Chief Judicial Magistrate's court rejected his application seeking registration of an FIR against the Congress MP on October 17, 2025. On July 9, a sessions court also dismissed Mishra's petition following which he challenged both orders in the high court.The controversy erupted after Rahul Gandhi said in Washington DC on September 10, 2024: "The fight is about whether a Sikh is going to be allowed to wear his turban or a kada in India.Or he, as a Sikh, is going to be able to go to Gurdwara. That's what the fight is about, and not just for him, but for all religions."Amid criticism of his remarks by the BJP, Rahul Gandhi hit back at the ruling party, accusing it of "resorting to lies" over his remarks and claiming that it was "unable to accept the truth.""The BJP has been spreading lies about my remarks in America. I want to ask every Sikh brother and sister in India and abroad - is there anything wrong in what I have said? Shouldn't India be a country where every Sikh - and every Indian - can freely practice their religion without fear?" the Lok Sabha leader of the opposition posted on X."As usual, the BJP is resorting to lies. They are desperate to silence me because they cannot stand the truth. But I will always speak up for the values that define India: our unity in diversity, equality, and love," he added.
Article Summary: The Allahabad high court declined to interfere with a Varanasi court order rejecting a plea seeking registration of an FIR against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. Justice Vikram D Chauhan dismissed the application filed by the petitioner, Nageshwar Mishra, observing that the allegation against Rahul Gandhi was based solely on newspaper reports.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: “I'm not the type of person to ignore that”: How motherhood changed Naomi Osaka’s priorities as the four-time Grand Slam champion admits her daughter could decide her tennis future
Article Text:
How motherhood changed Naomi Osaka’s priorities as the four-time Grand Slam champion admits her daughter could decide her tennis future

Naomi Osaka puts daughter Shai ahead of her tennis ambitions

Motherhood has changed how Naomi Osaka sees her future

Naomi Osaka has spent years chasing tennis history. She has won four Grand Slam titles, reached the top of the world rankings and built a career many players dream of. But today, the former world No. 1 has a different priority. Her three-year daughter, Shai, could have a say in how long she continues playing tennis. And Osaka has made it clear that she would not ignore her daughter's feelings just to stay in the sport.The Japanese tennis star opened up about motherhood and her uncertain future while speaking ahead of the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo on October 25, 2026. Her comments offered a glimpse into how much her life has changed since becoming a mother. Even with more tennis goals ahead, Osaka is prepared to make a difficult choice if her daughter wants her to spend less time travelling.For Osaka, the biggest question about her future may not involve another Grand Slam title or her world ranking. It may come from a conversation with her daughter.Speaking to reporters in Tokyo on October 25, Osaka admitted that she often thinks about how much longer she wants to play.She also explained that Shai's feelings could influence that decision."If my daughter did say she didn't want me to travel as much, I'm not the type of person to ignore that," Osaka said.It was a telling admission from a player who has spent much of her adult life competing at the highest level. The 29-year-old has won four major singles titles, including the US Open in 2018 and 2020 and the Australian Open in 2019 and 2021.However, motherhood has given her a different perspective. Osaka returned to tennis in 2023 after taking 15 months away from the sport following Shai's birth. Her comeback has involved balancing professional commitments with the demands of raising a young child.She also made it clear that tennis no longer takes up every part of her day."I wouldn't say I'm part-timing it but my entire day doesn't consist of that," she explained.Osaka added that she remains proud of her progress because she cannot dedicate all her time to tennis as she once did.Osaka's comments also connect to an earlier chapter of her career. In 2021, she stepped away from tennis to focus on her mental health. She later returned to the sport, but her priorities have continued to evolve.Now, Shai sits at the centre of those decisions."My daughter is my biggest priority," Osaka said during her Tokyo media appearance. She also admitted that balancing life as a professional player and a mother is something she is still learning little by little.That does not mean Osaka has lost her desire to compete. In fact, she sounded hopeful about her tennis future. During the same interaction, she said she was not far from finding her best form and felt optimistic about 2027.The four-time Grand Slam champion still has plenty she wants to achieve on court. Yet her latest admission shows that another tournament win may not always come first.In Osaka’s case, the decision to continue playing will involve more than her own ambitions. If Shai eventually asks her mother to spend more time at home, she has already made one thing clear: she will listen.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka has won four Grand Slam titles and reached the top of the world rankings. But the 29-year-old admits her daughter, Shai, could decide her tennis future. The former world No. 1 admits she often thinks about how much longer she wants to play. Osaka returned to tennis in 2023 after taking 15 months off following Shai's birth.

Article Title: Ollie Watkins’ wife Ellie returns to UK with children amid Saudi Arabia security fears after £50M transfer

Ollie Watkins continues Al-Hilal career after £50M Aston Villa exit

Ollie Watkins’ big-money move to Saudi Arabia was supposed to mark an exciting new chapter for his family. Just months after leaving Aston Villa for Al-Hilal, however, the England striker is facing an unexpected change at home. His wife, Ellie Watkins, has returned to the UK with their two young children amid growing security concerns in Saudi Arabia. The decision has left the family temporarily living in two countries, while Watkins continues his football career in Riyadh. Ellie has now opened up about the sudden change through a candid TikTok update.Ellie Watkins explained that the family's plans had changed after the situation in Saudi Arabia became increasingly concerning. In her TikTok video, she did not announce a permanent departure but made it clear that she had no fixed date for returning."We've had a bit of a plot twist"She then explained the reason behind the decision, saying:"I have come back to the UK for, hopefully, a little bit. I don't actually know when."The move comes amid renewed regional tensions and security concerns following deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia. A Houthi missile strike at Riyadh's airport in October reportedly killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.Another attack at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam also claimed two lives.Ellie addressed the situation directly in her video."There's just a little bit of conflict and things going on over in Saudi and we basically decided just to stay here until it calms down."For the couple, the decision appears to be centred on giving their children a more settled environment rather than making an immediate change to Watkins' professional commitments."I felt like I needed to do that for the kids so there is some form of normality until we can get back out there and all be together."While Ellie Watkins and the children have returned to Britain, Watkins remains in Saudi Arabia to continue playing for Al-Hilal.The £50 million-plus transfer from Aston Villa was one of the notable moves of the summer. It also marked a major change for the striker, who had spent several successful seasons in English football before accepting the opportunity in the Saudi Pro League.His performances have given Al-Hilal reasons to be pleased with the signing. The 2027 AFC Asian Cup, which the country was due to host in January, has been postponed until December 2027. Several other sporting events have also faced disruption, including the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition.For now, Watkins faces the challenge of balancing his new career with family life across two countries. Ellie has not given a date for their return, leaving their reunion dependent on how the situation develops.
Article Summary: Ollie Watkins left Aston Villa for Al-Hilal in a £50m transfer this summer. His wife, Ellie, has returned to the UK with their two young children. The decision comes amid growing security concerns in Saudi Arabia. Ellie Watkins has not given a date for their return.

Article Title: ‘Conditions are going to be a lot more similar’: Shubman Gill reveals why NZ ODI series is crucial for India's 2027 World Cup plans
Article Text:
Shubman Gill, Gautam Gambhir

Gill explains early arrival in New Zealand

Gill credits T20I series win for India's momentum

India captain Shubman Gill believes the ongoing ODI series against New Zealand could play an important role in the team's preparations for next year's World Cup, with the conditions during the current tour expected to offer a glimpse of what awaits them at the global tournament.With the World Cup scheduled for October-November next year, Gill feels playing in New Zealand in early November will give the Indian players a chance to experience conditions similar to those they could encounter during the competition.Gill pointed out that India's previous tours of New Zealand, South Africa and Australia have generally taken place in December and January, making the timing of the current series particularly useful.“The conditions that we’re going to get here are going to be a lot more similar to the ones that we’re going to get in the World Cup, especially playing here in early November. Usually, whenever we play in South Africa or in New Zealand or in Australia, we play around December, January and the World Cup being in October and November, so I think the conditions are going to be a lot more similar, and it’s going to be a really good experience for us,” Gill said in a video released by BCCI on X.India have already taken a 1-0 advantage in the five-match ODI series following their victory in the rain-hit opening match in Auckland on Wednesday. The visitors successfully chased a revised DLS target of 143 to get their campaign off to a winning start.However, the weather could again have a say in the second encounter, with rain forecast in Wellington on Saturday.The India skipper also spoke about his decision to arrive ahead of the rest of the squad. Gill wanted additional practice time, particularly with the red ball, as he looked to get a better understanding of the conditions in the country.The batter admitted that he had limited experience playing Test cricket in New Zealand and wanted to use the extra sessions to work on his game.“I wanted to get four or five extra sessions before I joined the team, mainly because of the red ball. I wanted to come here, work a little bit on my game, and see how the red ball is because I haven’t played a Test match here. I’ve played a couple of India A matches but haven’t really played that much Test cricket here,” Gill said.Gill also expressed confidence in India's fast-bowling resources, backing Anshul Kamboj, Aaqib Nabi Dar, Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh to make an impact during the series.He believes the conditions in New Zealand, particularly the bounce on offer, suit the qualities these pacers bring to the attack.“With the wickets seeming around and giving good bounce, our fast bowlers, whether it is Anshul, Aqib, Gurnoor or Arshdeep, I think the skill set that they bring to the team in these conditions is tailor-made for them, and I’m really optimistic that they’re going to have a really good series,” he said.Gill also reflected on India's 3-2 victory in the preceding T20I series, praising Shreyas Iyer 's captaincy and the team's ability to recover from difficult situations in the first two matches.He felt those comebacks helped India build momentum, which the team carried into the ODI series. Gill also acknowledged that New Zealand would be keen to respond after losing the T20I series."I think he (Shreyas) led the T20 series beautifully. You know, playing in a country like New Zealand and winning the first three matches is never easy, and more so the kind of situation we were in, in the first and in the second T20, from there making a comeback. You know, those are the kind of matches that completely change the momentum, and now the momentum is with us, having won that series, and a lot of our boxes are ticked, and New Zealand would look to come hard at us, which I think we are well prepared for," he said.India will now look to extend their advantage in the five-match ODI series when they take on New Zealand in Wellington on Saturday.
Article Summary: India captain Shubman Gill believes the current ODI series could play an important role in the team's preparations for next year's World Cup. Gill feels playing in New Zealand in early November will give the Indian players a chance to experience conditions similar to those they could encounter during the competition. India have already taken a 1-0 advantage in the five-match series following their victory in the rain-hit opening match.

A stunning catch from Sarfaraz Khan helped Mumbai break a 167-run partnership and turn the match on ite head in the final hour as the 42-time champions defeated Railways by 106 runs in their Ranji Trophy Group D clash on Thursday.Railways were firmly in the contest for much of the final day, thanks to centuries from opener Eshaan Goyal (103) and No. 7 batter Zubair Ali (115). The pair had kept Mumbai waiting for 156 minutes, facing 212 balls and adding 167 runs for the sixth wicket. However, Sarfaraz's effort in the field opened the door for Mumbai, who picked up their fourth outright win of the season to finish the first round with 27 points.Sarfaraz, who had earlier effected a run-out and dropped a catch, produced the moment that changed the game. Goyal attempted a sweep against Musheer Khan (3/42) but got a top edge. Standing at first slip, Sarfaraz covered the ground towards leg slip, dived full length and completed the catch to end the partnership.The India batter celebrated by running hard and throwing his arm in the air, with his effort even prompting the physio to come onto the field.Mumbai then struck twice more to put the result beyond Railways. India all-rounder Suryansh Shedge ran several yards to his left from mid-off to dismiss Zubair off Musheer, before Tanush Kotian (2/93) took a one-handed catch at short midwicket to remove the eighth batter.Railways were eventually bowled out for 265, with the collapse coming in a frantic final hour after the drinks break.The day had begun with Mumbai adding 60 runs to their overnight lead and setting Railways a target of 372. Divyaansh Saxena, who was unbeaten overnight, remained not out on 100 off 136 balls, hitting eight fours and a six.Railways' chase got off to a difficult start as Shams Mulani (4/69) picked up three wickets and Sarfaraz effected a run-out to leave them at 83/5. Goyal and Zubair then joined forces and appeared to have taken the game towards a draw before Mumbai's late fightback.Mumbai captain Siddesh Lad admitted that the possibility of a draw had crossed their minds, given the team's previous experience in the Irani Cup.“That (a draw) was always on the back of mind, because we had won the first innings and we have bad memories of CCI; we had lost the Irani Trophy on the last day of the match,” Lad told reporters.Mumbai finished the first round with 27 points, the highest tally among all teams. However, Lad said the team was not looking to be satisfied with its performance so far.“Last two seasons (also), we did really well in the league stage. But we don't want to be satisfied with what we have done in the first four games. We have a long journey ahead and we want to do something special -- add something to the legacy of Mumbai this season,” he said.
Article Summary: Mumbai beat Railways by 106 runs in their Ranji Trophy Group D clash. Sarfaraz Khan's stunning catch helped Mumbai break a 167-run partnership. Eshaan Goyal (103) and Zubair Ali (115) had put on 167 for the sixth wicket.

Spokespeople for both stars said their legal teams sent the orders. Both want their likenesses removed.The video, posted on X, showed a player in a No. 23 jersey with “Bron” on the back placing wagers on NBA players. Doncic’s name and image appeared on the phone screen. By Thursday afternoon, the post had been taken down.The demand is simple. Both stars want their names and likenesses out of the app’s marketing. The letters went to PlayVision Inc., the sports technology startup that owns Bron AI. James moved first, with his legal team calling for the ad to be removed. The Lakers star’s attorneys followed hours later with their own warning.The video leaned on James in several ways. Besides the jersey, it used an AI-generated voice that sounded like the 76ers star. Giannis Antetokounmpo, Donovan Mitchell and Dillon Brooks also appeared in the ad.The posts pulled in more than 900,000 views in under 24 hours. X removed them after Front Office Sports first reported the cease-and-desist.James left the Lakers for the 76ers in free agency this summer, so the two are no longer teammates. Doncic’s side still matched the move within hours. On the court, Doncic is averaging 38.5 points and the Lakers are 7-2, while James’ 76ers hold the league’s best record at 8-1.Adam Mendelsohn, James’ spokesperson, called the ad another sign of weak originality in sports marketing. He said the goal was probably to draw a cease-and-desist and turn the video into a story. A response is not optional in a case like this, he added, and it will not be the last of its kind. Mendelsohn said “these gimmicks never work because people see through it.”Lara Beth Seager, Doncic’s business manager, spoke more about the wider trend. She said cases like this are rising as AI tools get easier to use, calling it “something we’re dealing with more and more.” In her statement to The Athletic, she said her team will act each time Doncic’s name or likeness is used without permission.
Article Summary: LeBron James and Luka Doncic have each sent a cease-and-desist letter to the company behind Bron AI. Both stars want their names and likenesses out of the app’s marketing. The video, posted on X, showed a player in a No. 23 jersey with “Bron” on the back placing wagers on NBA players.

Article Title: Caitlin Clark makes history off the court as Dick’s Sporting Goods and Foot Locker choose WNBA superstar for a first-ever partnership
Article Text:
Caitlin Clark makes history off the court as Dick’s Sporting Goods and Foot Locker choose WNBA superstar for a first-ever partnership(Image via Getty: Caitlin Clark)

Caitlin Clark becomes the first athlete to partner with Dick’s Sporting Goods and Foot Locker

Nike's Caitlin 1 launch adds another milestone to her growing commercial success

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Caitlin Clark has added another major milestone to her growing basketball career, but this time, the Indiana Fever star has made headlines off the court. The WNBA superstar has signed a multi-year partnership with Dick’s Sporting Goods and Foot Locker, becoming the first individual athlete to earn the brand-partner title with either retailer.The agreement gives Clark a bigger platform in the sports retail business. It also brings together her growing signature product line and two major names in the sporting goods and sneaker industry.The agreement is not limited to putting Clark in a few advertisements. Dick’s Sporting Goods and Foot Locker will work with the Indiana Fever guard on national and global marketing campaigns, product promotions, retail experiences, digital campaigns, fan activations and community programming.The partnership will also support Clark’s signature footwear, apparel and other product lines. She will take part in appearances and community events, giving fans more opportunities to connect with the basketball star away from the court.There is also a personal connection behind the deal. Clark grew up shopping at Dick’s Sporting Goods before the start of each sports season. At the partnership announcement event in New York, she spoke about how the retailer had been part of her childhood sporting routine.“Dick’s Sporting Goods was always a stop before the start of any sports season when I was growing up,” Clark said in the statement announcing the partnership.She also called becoming the first brand partner for both companies a special full-circle moment. For Clark, the agreement brings her back to a retailer she knew long before she became one of basketball's biggest names.Dick’s executive chairman Ed Stack also highlighted Clark's appeal beyond basketball. In the announcement, he pointed to her interest in golf, football, soccer, baseball and softball, saying she could connect with fans across different parts of the company's business.The arrangement also reflects a new chapter for Dick’s Inc. The company owns the Foot Locker business, making this its first joint athlete partnership across the two retail brands. While both retailers have previously featured athletes in advertising campaigns and store events, neither had appointed an individual athlete as an official brand partner.The new agreement comes shortly after another major achievement for Clark. On October 1, 2026, Nike launched the Caitlin 1, her first signature basketball shoe, alongside an 18-piece apparel collection.The release marked the largest women's signature shoe launch in Nike's history. Demand quickly followed, with several sizes selling out within hours on Nike.com and other sneaker retail websites. The launch gave Clark another major presence in the footwear market, beyond her performances with the Indiana Fever.Her relationship with Nike also has a long history. Clark signed a name, image and likeness deal with the company in 2022 while playing college basketball. After entering the WNBA, she signed an eight-year, $28 million contract with Nike, which WWD reported as the largest deal of its kind for a women's basketball player.However, Nike is not the only major brand in her portfolio. Clark also has endorsement partnerships with Wilson, Gatorade, State Farm and Panini. The Dick’s Sporting Goods and Foot Locker agreement now adds two major retail platforms to that list.Her appeal also extends beyond her individual endorsements. A SportsPro marketability ranking released in November 2026 placed Clark at No. 1 among WNBA players and No. 15 among athletes worldwide.Dick’s executives also see an opportunity to connect Clark's popularity with the next generation of athletes. Emily Silver, the company's chief marketing, e-commerce and athlete experience officer, highlighted how Clark has inspired young girls and boys to take up sports.Foot Locker's senior vice president and chief marketing officer, Brett O’Brien, also praised her influence, saying she has brought new energy to basketball and inspired a new generation of fans.The partnership offers more than another addition to her endorsement portfolio. It connects Caitlin Clark's childhood experience as a young sports enthusiast with her present position as one of the most recognisable faces in women's basketball. And with Dick’s Sporting Goods and Foot Locker making her their first-ever athlete brand partner, the Indiana Fever star has reached another milestone that goes well beyond the WNBA court.
Article Summary: Caitlin Clark becomes the first athlete to partner with Dick’s Sporting Goods and Foot Locker. The agreement gives Clark a bigger platform in the sports retail business. It also brings together her growing signature product line and two major names in the sporting goods and sneaker industry.

Former India opener Kris Srikkanth has questioned Chennai Super Kings ' decision to trade for Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards, believing Sunrisers Hyderabad have emerged as the bigger winners from the four-player deal ahead of the IPL 2027 auction.CSK and SRH completed the trade on Thursday, with England all-rounder Livingstone and Australian seam-bowling all-rounder Edwards moving to the five-time champions. In exchange, India pacer Khaleel Ahmed and Australian fast bowler Nathan Ellis joined SRH.Reacting to the development on his YouTube channel, Srikkanth was particularly critical of CSK's decision to bring Edwards on board, describing the Australian as an ordinary bowler. He also questioned whether Livingstone would have a clear role in the Chennai side."Why Jack Edwards? He is an ordinary bowler. I am okay with CSK giving away Khaleel Ahmed as he's nothing great. This trade is a better one for SRH. Personally, I think Livingstone is a good cricketer if utilised well. But how he fits in with CSK is a big question mark. CSK should release Matt Short, who is a waste, and see if Livingstone can be an upgrade for him," said Srikkanth.Edwards, who made his international debut for Australia in January this year, will join CSK at his existing contract value of Rs 3 crore. SRH had signed him before his international debut, but the all-rounder did not get an opportunity to feature in IPL 2026 after a foot injury forced him out of the tournament.Livingstone, meanwhile, will move to CSK for Rs 6 crore, a significant reduction from the Rs 13 crore at which SRH had originally acquired him.Srikkanth's concerns about the deal also stem from the overseas-player combination available to CSK. With franchises permitted to field a maximum of four overseas players in their playing XI, he believes Livingstone could find it difficult to secure a regular place.The former India opener pointed out that CSK already have three overseas players who are likely to feature regularly, leaving limited room for the England all-rounder."CSK already have three sure starters among their overseas players in Dewald Brevis , Noor Ahmad and Jamie Overton. Article Title: Ex-KKR cricketer tests positive for cocaine, serves one-month suspension; here's what happened
Article Text:
Chris Lynn

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Australian batter Chris Lynn has served a one-month suspension after testing positive for cocaine during England's domestic T20 competition earlier this year. The 36-year-old, who was representing Northamptonshire in the T20 Blast, returned an adverse result following an anti-doping test conducted on Finals Day on July 18.England's Cricket Regulator confirmed on Thursday that Lynn had admitted to using cocaine outside competition and had subsequently completed a substance abuse treatment programme, which played a role in reducing his suspension from three months to one.Lynn underwent a routine anti-doping test after Northamptonshire secured the T20 Blast title for the third time. The Australian scored 39 and four in the two matches on Finals Day. His urine sample was later sent to a laboratory in France, where it tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.The batter travelled to Sri Lanka shortly after the tournament to participate in the Lanka Premier League (LPL). However, his campaign with Galle Gallants ended prematurely after he was ruled out on July 29 because of an unspecified leg injury, having featured in just one match.On July 31, Lynn was notified by the Cricket Regulator about the adverse analytical finding and was provisionally suspended.He subsequently admitted to cocaine use, confirming that it had taken place outside a sporting competition and had no connection with his cricketing performance.Lynn disclosed that the substance had been used "during a period of several hours across the evening of 15 July 2026 and into the early hours of 16 July 2026".Earlier on July 15, he had retired hurt during Northamptonshire's quarter-final win over Gloucestershire after being struck on the foot by a low full-toss from Duan Jansen.The Cricket Regulator initially brought two anti-doping charges against Lynn under the England and Wales Cricket Board's (ECB) regulations. However, one of the charges was later withdrawn after the cocaine concentration detected in his sample was found to be below the minimum threshold prescribed under World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) rules.Although the regulator initially proposed a three-month suspension, the punishment was reduced to one month after Lynn committed to a substance abuse treatment programme. The programme was completed on August 30, one month after his provisional suspension began.Lynn, who has represented Australia in four ODIs and 18 T20Is, has not played professional cricket since the start of his suspension. He is also yet to officially sign a contract with a franchise for the upcoming Big Bash League (BBL) season, although Australian media reports suggest he has agreed to join Melbourne Renegades.
Article Summary: Chris Lynn has served a one-month suspension after testing positive for cocaine. The 36-year-old was representing Northamptonshire in the T20 Blast. England's Cricket Regulator confirmed on Thursday that Lynn had admitted to using cocaine outside competition and had subsequently completed a substance abuse treatment programme.

Article Title: ‘Sarah stood by him as a pillar of support’: Bhatkal family celebrates Abdul El-Sayed’s US Senate win
Article Text:
Abdul El-Sayed achieved a significant milestone by winning the US Senate race in Michigan





MANGALURU: The Jukaku family, which has roots in Bhatkal in Uttara Kannada district, is in a celebratory mood following Abdul El-Sayed’s historic victory in the closely watched US Senate race in Michigan.El-Sayed, a doctor, defeated Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim elected to US Senate.The victory sparked celebrations in his in-law’s family back in Bhatkal from where his wife Dr Sarah Jukaku traces her roots.Sarah is the granddaughter of Jukaku Shamshuddin, who served as deputy minister for finance in the erstwhile Mysore State govt under chief minister BD Jatti.According to Sarah’s cousin, the family has been receiving congratulatory messages from people of Bhatkal.“It was a close fight marked by considerable hate and divisiveness, but the negative propaganda did not work. People stood united, and that is a big lesson and offers a new hope for India,” he said.“Sarah stood firmly by her husband as a pillar of support, and the couple worked tirelessly over the past 18 months. It was not an easy journey. However, El-Sayed stood his ground with honesty and conviction. The small donations and support he received also played a crucial role,” the cousin added.Several family members settled in the US travelled to Michigan to be part of the celebrations.The family’s WhatsApp group remained active throughout the night tracking the developments closely.
Article Summary: Abdul El-Sayed, a doctor, defeated Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim elected to US Senate. The victory sparked celebrations in his in-law’s family back in Bhatkal from where his wife Dr Sarah Jukaku traces her roots.

Article Title: Olympic gold, Asiad medals stolen from hockey legend MM Somaya's Bengaluru home
Article Text:
MM Somaya, a hockey legend, faced a devastating burglary at his home in Bengaluru on October 28.





BENGALURU: Last Wednesday, when hockey legend MM Somaya returned from his morning walk in Apangela, near his hometown Madikeri, his wife Shami greeted him with news of a burglary at their Bengaluru residence.His first thoughts were about his most prized possessions - medals won for the country, including his gold medal from 1980 Moscow Olympics. He rushed back to find his worst fears confirmed. His house in HAL 3rd Stage had been broken into between 2.30am and 4am on Oct 28, and valuables worth over Rs 3 lakh, including four international medals, were stolen."I'm obviously very hurt because the medals are an irreplaceable symbol of years of dedication, sacrifice and service to the country," an anguished Somaya told TOI.The two burglars, wearing helmets, also stole Rs 30,000 in cash and gold and silver articles. They entered after breaking open the main door and were captured on neighbours' CCTV cameras."Apart from the Olympic gold, two Asian Games medals - a silver from the 1982 Games in New Delhi and a bronze from the 1986 Games in Seoul - and a Champions Trophy bronze from 1982 were stolen," Somaya (67) added.Neighbours alerted the couple around 7.30am, and they immediately left for Bengaluru.Police registered an FIR the same day and said they were confident of solving the case, citing strong clues."We have collected much CCTV footage from the area and have some vital clues on the miscreants. They had watched the house for some hours and, after ensuring it was locked, broke in. However, we will crack the case," an investigating officer said.Somaya, a former India captain, moved to the city from Mumbai in 2025 after retiring from Bharat Petroleum.
Article Summary: MM Somaya's house in Bengaluru broken into between 2.30am and 4am on Oct 28. Valuables worth over Rs 3 lakh, including four international medals, were stolen. Two burglars, wearing helmets, also stole Rs 30,000 in cash and gold and silver articles.

Article Title: Hours after US mid-term election results, Elon Musk sends 'let's go to Space' message to Google, Amazon, Meta and other companies building data centres; says: Right now …
Article Text:
Elon Musk sends 'let's go to Space' message hours after mid-term election results

Democrats wins Texas

US mid-term election rewrites history

Hours after mid-term election results, Elon Musk said that building data centres in space look increasingly “appealing right now”. The post comes following the Democrats’ strong performance in the US mid-term elections. Musk, who has been a prominent Republican supporter during the election cycle and reportedly spent over $150 million in Texas alone, shared two posts on X (formerly Twitter). “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk wrote in the early hours of Wednesday, November 4, after election results pointed to a major victory for Democrats.“Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time 🤷‍♂️,” Musk said in the second post, appearing to joke about his political influence and the election outcome.The comments came as Democrats made significant gains, including a surprise victory in Texas’ governor’s race by Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who has opposed data centre expansion. Notably, Elon Musk and his companies – Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI have a growing footprint of high-performance computing (HPC), chip manufacturing, and data center-related infrastructure projects across Texas.Musk’s posts did not directly address companies such as Google , Amazon and Meta, which are expanding their data centre infrastructure to support AI development.The billionaire's remark on data centres come as the AI industry faces growing political scrutiny over massive data centers, with concerns about electricity costs and environmental impacts becoming campaign issues.The 2026 midterm elections in the US had a series of historic firsts so far. Voters elected the country's first Black woman governor, first Native American woman governor, first Native American woman senator and first openly gay male senator in the mid-term elections.The elections also set a records for women's political participation. According to Rutgers University's Center for American Women and Politics, nearly 300 women ran for the US House and Senate.
Article Summary: Elon Musk says data centres in space look 'appealing right now' Comments come as Democrats make significant gains in US mid-term elections. Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI have a growing footprint of high-performance computing (HPC) and data center-related infrastructure projects across Texas.

Article Title: Punjab fully prepared to host Hockey World Cup in 2030: CM Bhagwant Mann
Article Text:
Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann expressed confidence in hosting the Hockey World Cup in 2030





CHANDIGARH: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Thursday asserted that the state is now fully prepared to host the prestigious Hockey World Cup in 2030.Congratulating the people of Punjab on the successful organisation of the international tournament, Asian Champions Trophy, the chief minister said that the state's inseparable bond with hockey, its legacy of 77 Olympians and 48 Olympic medal winners, and its rapidly strengthening sports infrastructure make it a natural destination for major global sporting events.With six new hockey astroturf grounds already constructed, two more underway and Rs 1,744 crore earmarked exclusively for sports, Mann said the government is committed to taking Punjab's sporting legacy to greater heights.Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria and Mann congratulated the people of Punjab for scripting a new chapter in the state's sporting history by successfully hosting the Asian Champions Trophy Punjab 2026.India retained the coveted title by defeating Japan 4-1 in a thrilling final at the Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali.Addressing the gathering, Mann said Punjab is fully prepared to host the prestigious Hockey World Cup in 2030.He said the successful organising of the ongoing Asian Champions Trophy Punjab 2026 reflects the state's growing capability to host major international sporting events."Hosting the Asian Champions Trophy for the first time is a historic achievement in Punjab's sporting journey and a stepping stone towards bigger international sporting events. Punjab is globally renowned for its hardworking people, vibrant culture and warm hospitality."Every player and visitor will carry unforgettable memories of their stay in Punjab... Hockey and Punjab are inseparable, as it is almost impossible to imagine the glorious history of Indian hockey without the contribution of Punjabi players," Mann said.From legendary Olympians Balbir Singh Senior, Udham Singh, Prithipal Singh, Ajit Pal Singh and Surjit Singh to contemporary stars such as Harmanpreet Singh, Manpreet Singh, Mandeep Singh and Rupinder Pal Singh, Punjab has consistently supplied extraordinary talent to Indian hockey, said Mann.The chief minister said Punjab has produced 77 hockey Olympians from the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics to the 2024 Paris Olympics, while 48 players from the state have won Olympic medals. This extraordinary legacy reflects the deep-rooted passion for hockey in Punjab.He said, "Our government is committed to strengthening sporting infrastructure across Punjab. Six new hockey astroturf grounds have been constructed during our tenure, while work on two additional grounds is progressing."Besides this, 18 six-a-side astroturf hockey grounds have been established to promote the game at the grassroots level, he added.
Article Summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann expresses confidence in hosting the Hockey World Cup in 2030. Mann said Punjab is fully prepared to host the prestigious Hockey World World Cup. He said Punjab has produced 77 hockey Olympians from the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics to the 2024 Paris Olympics.

The latter becomes the subject of some obvious but well-timed jokes about the appearances of public personalities, including a remark that keeping one is “no longer an anti-national act”.Ghalib insists that the drivers take him to Ballimaran, where he famously lived, opening up further avenues for political digs. One offers to take him to the Ramlila ground instead, calling it the new protest site. But Ghalib is taken aback by both the suggestion and the fare – ₹100, ₹200, ₹500 to travel from one part of Delhi to another? For ₹5, he could have reached his hometown, Agra! The drivers scoff at his suggestion, while he mocks their language, saying, “The jokes, digs and puns are topical and sharp, blending seamlessly into the drama.Writer-director and actor M Sayeed Alam is incredible as Ghalib, with one of the play’s most memorable lighter moments coming when he tries to teach a driver how to pronounce Jama Masjid.Much of the drama’s strength lies in its use of timely political and NCR references to draw humour from Ghalib’s bewilderment. Amid the quickfire jokes, Ghalib also offers a lovely line on the beauty and impact of silence, contrasting the play’s humour with the lyricism of his works.The final two acts see Ghalib finally embracing the ‘new’ Delhi. He changes his get-up, adopts athleisure and swaps his cherished maroon tin suitcase for a tennis racket. The few actors in the play do more than a decent job, but much of its weight rests on Alam’s performance and vision, which he brings to life with easy charm.-Anvita Singh
Article Summary: Born on December 27, 1797, the beloved Urdu poet finds himself transported to New Delhi in 2026. Writer-director and actor M Sayeed Alam is incredible as Ghalib. The few actors in the play do more than a decent job, but much of its weight rests on Alam’s performance.

Article Text: For young Mumbaikars, Diwali preparations begin long before the first diya is lit. Article Title: Historian Vasantrao More, director Sharad Bhutadiya win ‘Brand Kolhapur’ Lifetime Achievement award
Article Text:
Brand Kolhapur award winners along with renowned author Vishwas Patil and MLC Satej Patil

Kolhapur

:





Eminent historian and author Dr Vasantrao More and veteran theatre artist and director Dr Sharad Bhutadiya were honoured with the ‘Brand Kolhapur’ Lifetime Achievement Awards on Wednesday in a coveted event.The ‘Brand Kolhapur’ awards were instituted to recognise distinguished individuals from the district who have brought national and international recognition to the region through their achievements in fields of art, sports, education and culture. This was the seventh edition of the awards ceremony. The event was held at Megh Malhar Hall at Hotel Sayaji in the presence of renowned author Vishwas Patil , best known for his book ‘Panipat’, and the Leader of Opposition for the Congress party in Legislative Council, MLC Satej Patil Lawn tennis player Sandesh Kurale and rifle shooter Sonam Maskar were awarded the Host Brand Kolhapur Award 2026. Other awardees incldued Rohit Malvekar, Harshvardhan Patil, Vaibhavi Chavan, Juhi Dharwade, Dr Nandita Paranjape-Joshi, Dr Rishikesh Pol, Dr Mahesh Shinde, Pooja Pavaskar, Shubham Sutar, Rohit Chavan, Amrita Pujari, Sanika Mane, Vishwajit More, Shambavi Kshirsagar, Jijau Patil, Monica Ekal, Swapnali Magdum, Sai Jadhav, Jitendra Karambe, Vedanthi Mangutkar, Hrishikesh Kabanurkar, Rutuja Guruv, Rishikesh Alase, Prathamesh Shinde, Pandurang Phonde, Madhurima Sawant, Gaurav Patil, Aditya Jadhav, Tanvi Magdum and Deven Mahendra Pawar .Speaking on the occasion, MLC Satej Patil said, “This initiative is taken intentionally during Diwali as these rising talent from Kolhapur who are shining on national and international level arrive to their native place during Diwali festival. Son of soil of Kolhapur, who are former or current bureaucrats or have worked on higher authority are invited as chief guest. Till date, Dr Dnyaneshwar Mule, Bhushan Gagrani, Vikas Kharge, Hemant Nimbalkar, Sunil Limaye, Dr Yashwantrao Thorat and this year Vishwas Patil have marked their presence as chief guests. ”
Article Summary: The ‘Brand Kolhapur’ awards were instituted to recognise distinguished individuals from the district who have brought national and international recognition to the region.
